content:
Iris: customer ask from Acme: want per-route throughput caps and ability to buy per-route add-ons. they run high-throughput ingestion routes and prefer separate billing for that pipeline. can we support per-route entitlements?

Tom: technically doable but complexity multiplies. we'll need per-route tokens counters and separate pricing SKUs. routing will need to respect route-level overrides.

Diego: sales angle: large customers like per-route billing because they can charge back internally. Suggest offering per-route as part of Dedicated/Latency Lane only.

Iris: tradeoffs: per-route billing increases overhead for quota UI and support. also need a way to export route-level invoices.

mktg-bot: create campaign: "Chargeback-ready routing" for enterprise GTM.

finance-bot: require projected uplift and complexity cost. need to run a TCO analysis before greenlighting.

Tom: propose MVP: route-label on requests, tenant-level purchase of per-route add-on that maps label -> credits. enforcement: token deduction from route credit pool, fall back to tenant pool.

Iris: contract language: "Customers can allocate purchased route credits to named routes. Unused route credits roll up to tenant balance at month-end."

Diego: GTM: pilot with one enterprise (Acme) paid PoC. include route-level dashboards and exportable CSV.

Iris: infra asks: need tagging, credits accounting, and invoice export. Data retention for route billing should be 13 months.

Tom: implement ticket INF-901 for route-level accounting. ETA: spec next week.

finance-bot: scheduled TCO analysis for Friday.

Iris: launch criteria: 1) route labeling in SDKs & Console 2) per-route credit accounting 3) invoice export 4) legal + finance sign-off 5) pilot conversion 2 customers.

Diego: adding to roadmap. will align legal & sales engineering.

Iris: action items: Iris to capture spec, Tom to own INF-901, Diego to lock Acme pilot.

Tom: ack.
